eyebrow: Integrated iron & steel value chain · planned upstream development
headline: FROM TANZANIAN IRON ORE TO METALLURGICAL-GRADE RAW MATERIALS
introduction: Chalinze Steel Mills Ltd is developing an integrated upstream operation that transforms Tanzania's Run-of-Mine (ROM) iron ore into carefully prepared, quality-controlled iron-bearing materials — calibrated lump ore, beneficiated iron ore concentrate, sinter feed and iron ore pellets — that form the essential foundation for downstream ironmaking and steel production.
valueStatement: The upstream operation is designed to establish a reliable, consistent and quality-controlled raw-material supply. Downstream ironmaking, steelmaking and steel products are the intended impact of this upstream investment; they are not yet in operation at Chalinze Steel Mills Ltd.

stages.title: IRON ORE MINING
stages.status: Planned upstream operation · mine and supply details to confirm
stages.description: Extraction of iron-bearing minerals through open-pit or underground mining, including drilling, blasting, excavation, loading and haulage of Run-of-Mine (ROM) ore. This first upstream stage establishes the raw-material foundation for the proposed iron and steel value chain. Mine ownership, permits, reserves, supply agreements and current extraction are not confirmed.
stages.input: Natural iron-ore deposits (resource and supply to confirm)
stages.machinery: Drilling rigs, excavators, loaders and haul trucks are the typical equipment class; the final mine fleet and mine plan are not confirmed.
stages.technical: No ore assay, resource estimate, reserve, mine permit, production rate or supply agreement has been supplied for publication.

hotspots.label: Mineral resource
hotspots.detail: Resource identification is part of the project concept. An approved geological resource statement and supporting assays have not been supplied.

hotspots.label: Material handling
hotspots.detail: Ore loading and haulage toward processing are conceptual material-flow steps, not verified installed equipment.

stages.title: CRUSHING & SCREENING
stages.description: Reduction of the extracted ore into controlled particle sizes through primary, secondary and tertiary crushing, followed by screening and classification. The objective is to produce a consistent, correctly sized feed for the selected downstream processing route.
stages.output: Crushed and screened iron ore of controlled particle size
stages.machinery: Jaw, gyratory and cone crushers with vibrating screens and classifiers; final equipment selection and duty are not confirmed.
stages.technical: No throughput, reduction ratio, particle-size target or equipment specification is asserted.

hotspots.label: Size reduction
hotspots.detail: Crushing stages illustrate progressive particle-size reduction; installed equipment and sizing strategy have not been confirmed.

hotspots.label: Screening & classification
hotspots.detail: Screening separates material by size. Cut sizes and screening efficiency depend on the approved process design.

stages.title: ORE BENEFICIATION & CONCENTRATION
stages.description: Physical processing to improve iron content and reduce unwanted gangue minerals and impurities through grinding, magnetic separation, gravity separation, flotation and other suitable technologies. The final beneficiation route depends on the ore's mineralogical composition.
stages.machinery: SAG mills, ball mills and HPGR for grinding; magnetic and gravity separators and flotation cells for separation. Technology selection is not finalised.
stages.technical: No iron grade, concentrate specification, recovery rate, process yield or water balance is asserted.

hotspots.label: Grinding & liberation
hotspots.detail: Grinding liberates iron-bearing minerals from gangue; mill selection and energy demand remain subject to design.

hotspots.label: Mineral separation
hotspots.detail: Separation illustrates the principle of upgrading iron-bearing material. No specific technology, recovery or concentrate grade is claimed.

stages.title: DEWATERING & MATERIAL HANDLING
stages.description: Thickening, filtration, moisture control, stockpiling and blending to achieve consistent concentrate quality and prepare materials for subsequent processing. This stage stabilises the concentrate before agglomeration or dispatch.
stages.machinery: Thickeners, filter presses and vacuum filters, with conveyors, stackers, reclaimers and feeders; capacities are not confirmed.
stages.technical: No moisture target, filtration rate, stockpile capacity or blending specification is supplied.

hotspots.label: Dewatering
hotspots.detail: Thickening and filtration reduce moisture for handling and further processing; equipment duty is not specified.

hotspots.label: Blending & stockpiling
hotspots.detail: Blending and stockpiling aim for consistent feed quality; no capacity or homogenisation result is claimed.

stages.title: AGGLOMERATION & PELLETIZING
stages.description: Conversion of fine iron ore concentrates into stronger, uniformly sized agglomerates through pelletising and induration, or sintering where the selected ironmaking route requires it. Not every ore or ironmaking route requires agglomeration; the need is confirmed through process selection.
stages.output: Iron ore pellets or sinter feed (agglomerated iron-bearing material)
stages.machinery: Disc or drum pelletisers and induration furnaces, or sintering machines where required; final configuration is not selected.
stages.technical: Whether agglomeration is required, and the choice between pellets and sinter, depend on mineralogical characterisation, metallurgical testing and the selected ironmaking technology.

hotspots.label: Pelletising & induration
hotspots.detail: Pellets are formed from fine concentrate and hardened by induration; the circuit is conceptual and route-dependent.

hotspots.label: Sintering option
hotspots.detail: Sintering is an alternative agglomeration route where the ironmaking configuration requires sinter feed rather than pellets.

stages.title: STOCKPILING, BLENDING & DISPATCH
stages.status: Planned upstream output · dispatch framework to confirm
stages.description: Quality-controlled storage, blending, sampling and dispatch of prepared iron-bearing materials to downstream ironmaking facilities. This is the final upstream stage, delivering consistent, metallurgical-grade feedstock and marking the boundary where the upstream operation ends and downstream processing begins.
stages.input: Prepared iron-bearing materials (lump ore, concentrate, sinter feed or pellets)
stages.output: Quality-controlled iron-bearing feedstock dispatched to downstream ironmaking
stages.machinery: Conveyors, stackers, reclaimers and feeders, with sampling systems, laboratories and analysers; capacities are representative only.
stages.technical: No stockpile capacity, sampling standard, product specification, logistics partner or delivery schedule has been verified.

hotspots.label: Sampling & quality control
hotspots.detail: Sampling and laboratory analysis support consistent feedstock quality; no standard or result is asserted.

hotspots.label: Dispatch boundary
hotspots.detail: Dispatch marks the upstream output boundary. Downstream ironmaking and steelmaking are not yet in operation at Chalinze.

quality.title: Incoming material
quality.detail: Assess raw-material identity, physical characteristics and chemical composition against criteria approved by the project.

quality.title: Size control
quality.detail: Monitor particle-size distribution and screening efficiency to maintain a consistent feed. No numerical target is supplied.

quality.title: Concentrate grade
quality.detail: Monitor iron content and the reduction of gangue and impurities. No concentrate specification or recovery target is asserted.

quality.title: Moisture & consistency
quality.detail: Control moisture and blending consistency so the concentrate is stable for agglomeration or dispatch.

quality.title: Agglomerate quality
quality.detail: Monitor pellet or sinter strength, sizing and consistency where agglomeration is part of the selected route.

quality.title: Dispatch & traceability
quality.detail: Sampling, product identification and traceability support quality-controlled dispatch of prepared feedstock to downstream facilities.

billet.name: Steel billets
billet.description: Steel billets are a downstream product, produced by downstream ironmaking, steelmaking and continuous casting. Chalinze Steel Mills Ltd has not started downstream production: billets are shown as the intended downstream output that the planned upstream iron-bearing feedstock is designed to supply.

billet.specificationNote: Grades, chemistry, length, weight, tolerances, standards, production volumes and availability have not been supplied. Cross-sections require final engineering confirmation. Downstream production is not yet in operation.

downstream.name: Reinforcement steel bars (rebar)
downstream.description: Rebar is a primary downstream product made by rolling billet feedstock into reinforcing bars for reinforced-concrete construction.
downstream.applications: Buildings, bridges, roads, dams and other infrastructure.

downstream.name: Steel wire rods
downstream.description: Wire rods are primary rolled products made directly from billet feedstock and can supply further wire drawing and processing.
downstream.applications: Feedstock for wire drawing, nails, binding wire, fencing, mesh and fasteners.

downstream.name: Steel round bars
downstream.description: Round bars are primary rolled products that may be produced from steel billets for engineering and industrial use.
downstream.applications: Engineering, machinery, fabrication and industrial applications.

downstream.name: Steel flat bars & square bars
downstream.description: Flat and square bars are primary rolled products shaped from billet feedstock.

downstream.name: Structural steel sections
downstream.description: Structural sections are primary rolled products; examples include angles, channels and other steel sections.
downstream.applications: Industrial structures, buildings, towers and infrastructure.

downstream.name: Merchant bars
downstream.description: Merchant bars are a broader category of primary rolled long products made from billet feedstock.
downstream.applications: Potential use in general metalworking and fabrication.

downstream.name: Drawn steel wire
downstream.description: Steel wire is a secondary product made by drawing wire rods to smaller diameters; it is further processing of a rolled product rather than direct billet rolling.
downstream.applications: Feedstock for wire goods, fasteners, fencing and other fabricated products.

downstream.name: Nails & fasteners
downstream.description: Nails and fasteners are further-processed products commonly made from drawn wire or other suitable processed steel feedstock.
downstream.applications: Construction, furniture, manufacturing and general fastening.

downstream.name: Binding wire
downstream.description: Binding wire is a secondary wire product made from processed steel wire, not necessarily directly from billets.
downstream.applications: Tying and securing reinforcement and general construction uses.

downstream.name: Fencing products
downstream.description: Fencing is manufactured through further processing and forming of steel wire or other suitable feedstock.

downstream.name: Welded wire mesh
downstream.description: Welded wire mesh is a secondary downstream product made by forming processed steel wire into a grid and joining intersections; it does not necessarily use billets directly.
downstream.applications: Reinforcement in concrete slabs, pavements, walls and precast elements.

downstream.name: Industrial steel components
downstream.description: Billets may supply downstream facilities that further process steel into industrial components.
downstream.applications: Components are shaped and finished by specialist downstream manufacturers.

downstream.name: Fabricated steel products
downstream.description: Fabricators can transform processed steel sections into assemblies and finished products.
downstream.applications: Cut, formed, joined or finished products made by downstream operators.

infrastructure.title: Materials handling
infrastructure.detail: The proposed upstream project discusses ore reception, conveying, process transfer, stockpiling and blending. Final layouts and equipment are subject to design.

infrastructure.title: Plant utilities

infrastructure.title: Automation & control
infrastructure.detail: Automation, process monitoring and digital manufacturing are described as technology themes, not as installed or operating systems.

infrastructure.title: Logistics & dispatch
infrastructure.detail: Internal material handling, stockpiling and dispatch of prepared feedstock are part of the proposed scope; delivery routes and operating capacity are not confirmed.

sustainability.title: Responsible development
sustainability.detail: Environmental, health, safety and community considerations are part of project development. No permit, assessment outcome or operating result is claimed here.

sustainability.title: Resource stewardship
sustainability.detail: The project brief discusses efficient use of materials, water and energy as design intentions. Quantified performance data has not been supplied.

sustainability.title: Emissions & energy
sustainability.detail: A low-carbon ambition appears in company materials and brand artwork; no verified emissions baseline, reduction, certification or operating performance is asserted.

industries.title: Construction & infrastructure
industries.detail: Downstream steel products may serve construction and public-infrastructure applications. Downstream production is not yet in operation.

industries.title: Mining & mineral processing
industries.detail: Steel materials can support equipment, plant and infrastructure needs in mining supply chains.

industries.title: Energy & utilities
industries.detail: Potential customer industries identified in company materials include energy and utility development.

industries.title: Manufacturing & fabrication
industries.detail: Steel processors, engineering firms and fabricators can further transform billet-derived products.

approvalNote: This page describes the proposed upstream concept. Technical routes, equipment, product specifications, project status and imagery require approval against current company and engineering information before publication. For an integrated iron and steel presentation, beneficiation and agglomeration are distinguished: not every ore deposit requires the same processing stages, and not every ironmaking route requires pellets. The final configuration should be established through mineralogical characterisation, metallurgical testing and technology selection.
